A grab-bag of capabilities and gotchas you'll reach for once the basics work.

Importing data

ATAK's import framework is pluggable. The simplest path is to broadcast an import intent and let ATAK auto-detect the content:

Intent i = new Intent(ImportExportMapComponent.ACTION_IMPORT_DATA);
i.putExtra(ImportReceiver.EXTRA_URI, Uri.fromFile(f).toString());
// optional: EXTRA_CONTENT, EXTRA_MIME_TYPE (else auto-discovered),
//           EXTRA_SHOW_NOTIFICATIONS, EXTRA_ZOOM_TO_FILE
AtakBroadcast.getInstance().sendBroadcast(i);

Either EXTRA_URI or EXTRA_URI_LIST is required; everything else is optional.

To teach ATAK a new content/MIME type, implement Importer + Marshal and register them: ImporterManager.registerImporter(...), MarshalManager.registerMarshal(...), and ImportExportMapComponent.getInstance().addImporterClasses(...).

IO Abstraction Layer

For plugins that need to mediate filesystem and database access (e.g. to add encryption), the IOProvider interface abstracts both java.io.File-style operations and SQLite database construction. Inject one via IOProviderFactory.registerProvider(...) (stack-based — unregisterProvider(...) pops and restores the previous one).

  • Databases are returned as DatabaseIface (close to Android's SQLiteDatabase), and ATAK's SQLite ships the SpatiaLite extension — a compliant provider must keep it available.
  • Only one provider is active at a time; switching providers clears state loaded under the previous one. Register custom providers early (in your lifecycle), before anything touches storage.

This is an advanced, whole-app hook — most plugins never need it.

Radial Menu API

You can build/compose radial menus in code: MapMenuWidget (a menu), MapMenuButtonWidget (a button), with button onClick behaviour assigned via objects implementing MapAction, and submenus assigned as nested MapMenuWidgets. XML menu assets remain fully supported (unchanged schema).

Layout is weight-driven (like Android's layout_weight): button spans come from the menu XML buttonSpan, or default to 1 for dynamically-added buttons — so mixing asset-defined and dynamic buttons needs matching weights. Menu geometry is controlled by startAngle (default -90, bottom), coveredAngle (default 360 for a primary menu), and clockwiseWinding (default counter-clockwise).

Map projections & coordinate transforms

ATAK displays two projections, both on the WGS84 datum: Equirectangular (EPSG:4326) for the flat map and ECEF (EPSG:4978) for the globe. Data is normalized to WGS84 on ingest (or reprojected at render) via Proj.4.

The com.atakmap.map.projection.Projection interface exposes the EPSG spatialReferenceID and forward / inverse transforms (WGS84 ↔ projection x/y/z). Get instances from ProjectionFactory; add your own by implementing ProjectionSpi.

Gotcha: use PluginSpinner, not android.widget.Spinner

A plain Android Spinner fails in a plugin because of how it uses its Context (the two-context problem again — see How ATAK plugins work). Use the drop-in replacement com.atakmap.android.gui.PluginSpinner:

  • In XML layouts: replace android.widget.Spinner with com.atakmap.android.gui.PluginSpinner.
  • In code: usage is identical to Spinner. Build the ArrayAdapter with the plugin context, set the dropdown view resource, then setAdapter(...).

(Several ATAK widgets have Plugin… variants for the same reason — reach for them when a stock widget misbehaves in a plugin.)

Working with native code (JNI/NDK)

Plugins can ship native libraries. ATAK includes native libs for x86, armeabi-v7a, arm64-v8a — target those ABIs. Native code that depends on ATAK's bundled shared objects must be built with NDK r12b (the version ATAK core uses); otherwise you may use a newer NDK.

  • Android loads native deps explicitly and in order (unlike desktop Java). Load each dependency before the library that needs it.
  • If you use **PluginNativeLoader**, call PluginNativeLoader.init(Context) with the plugin context before loading any library.
  • The hellojni example demonstrates building/deploying a JNI library in a plugin.

Release builds & obfuscation

Run ./gradlew assemble<Flavor>Release periodically during development — the release build is ProGuard-obfuscated and surfaces issues a debug build hides:

  • Account for all reflection in proguard-gradle.txt (keep rules).
  • Lambdas for ATAK inner interfaces are known to break under obfuscation — use explicit anonymous classes there.
  • Anything using gson or other serialization needs keep rules too.

Developing on an emulator

ATAK leans on hardware-accelerated graphics, so stock AVDs may not run it. Tips:

  • The emulator needs GLES 3.0+ (Settings → Advanced → Open GL ES API Level); on Windows the ANGLE renderer options tend to work best.
  • If a bad GPU choice stops it booting: emulator -avd <NAME> -gpu host.
  • DNS issues: emulator @<NAME> -dns-server 8.8.8.8.
  • If no AVD configuration works, the x86 Android VM (android-x86.org) is a viable alternative.
